statement: For a general quintic threefold over a field k of characteristic different from 2 and 5, the sum over its closed lines of the transferred quadratic types is 1445⟨1⟩+1430⟨−1⟩ in GW(k).

answer.qualification: Count closed lines with residue-field transfers. The Fermat calculation uses distinguished limiting lines under deformation, not a finite set of all lines on the special Fermat quintic.

source.location: Theorem 1.2 and equation (1) in the Introduction; Theorem 1.4 and Section 6.3 compute the dynamic Euler number

scope: Projective lines contained in a general quintic hypersurface X in P⁴. Count geometric lines, without parametrizations or markings. Generality includes a finite reduced Fano scheme; special smooth quintics, including the Fermat quintic, can have positive-dimensional line families and are not generic fibres. Real bounds concern regular real coefficient parameters. Enriched counts state their field-characteristic hypotheses.
notes:
Count closed lines with residue-field transfers. The Fermat calculation uses distinguished limiting lines under deformation, not a finite set of all lines on the special Fermat quintic.

Pauli, Remark 1.3, explicitly credits the GW-valued Euler-class computation to Levine, Example 8.2. Pauli’s new geometric interpretation in terms of line types and dynamic local contributions remains part of this record.

Related literature. Motivic Euler characteristics and Witt-valued characteristic classes (Marc Levine, 2019). Historical or related contributions are retained here. Their own precise statements have not been independently verified for a separate result in this migration.

Source discussion. For a general quintic threefold over a field k of characteristic different from 2 and 5, the sum over its closed lines of the transfers of their quadratic types equals 1445⟨1⟩+1430⟨−1⟩ in GW(k). The rank is 2875 and the real signature is 15.
